chunks: From him, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Muskan, from Ayyub ibn al-Hurr, who said:

Abu ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام was asked about a man who died while he was in a ship at sea: how should he be dealt with? He said: “He should be placed in a large jar, its opening should be sealed, and he should be cast into the water.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: If a Muslim man dies among disbelieving men and Muslim women among whom he has no mahram, then one of the disbelievers is instructed to perform ghusl, and he washes him with the women instructing him in the washing of the people of Islam. Likewise, if a Muslim woman dies among Muslim men among whom she has no mahram and disbelieving women, the men instruct one of those women to perform ghusl and teach her to wash her according to the sunnah of Islam. This is indicated by that.

key_terms.السَّفِينَةِ: the ship in which the deceased was present at sea
key_terms.الْبَحْرِ: the sea, indicating the exceptional circumstance of burial
key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: the ritual washing of the deceased
key_terms.خَابِيَةٍ: a large jar or vessel in which the body is placed
key_terms.سُنَّةِ الْإِسْلَامِ: the prescribed Islamic manner of washing the deceased
key_terms.مَحْرَمٌ: a person within prohibited degrees of marriage, allowing certain bodily handling
key_terms.يُوكَى: it is sealed or tied shut

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a Muslim dies at sea or among people who cannot directly perform the funeral washing?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses rulings concerning the handling and ghusl of the deceased in exceptional circumstances. It explains what is to be done when someone dies at sea and outlines how the deceased may be washed when only non-mahram Muslims and disbelievers are present.
